subject: Using multiple regions in fortify of SpatialPolygonsDataFrame?

messages.author: 146c5031f31e4913
messages.subject: Using multiple regions in fortify of SpatialPolygonsDataFrame?
parts:
Hi all, 

I'm using fortify + ldply to create a single data frame out of a series of shapefiles from Europe. When I'm working with the admin region 0 files (country borders), I can simply set region = "NAME_ENGLI" and I end up with an id column that lists the various country names. If I apply the same process to the admin region 2 files, and setting region = "NAME_2", then I get a data frame with the admin region 2 name in the id column.

europe_adm0 <- ldply(.data = adm0list, .fun = fortify, region = "NAME_ENGLI", .progress = "text")
europe_adm2 <- ldply(.data = adm2list, .fun = fortify, region = "NAME_2", .progress = "text")

Does anyone know how I could use multiple regions with the fortify function? For the admin region 2 data frame I would like to end up with both the admin region 2 name and the country name into the data frame. I would try a join, but in the resulting admin 2 data frame there isn't a column I could do the matching on. My first thought would be to write out a for loop which would apply fortify separately by country, but that seems like an inefficient way to handle this.  Is there a better way?

Thanks, 

- Jake
